title: Searching for Ganesha: Collecting Images of the Sweet-Loving, Elephant-Headed Hindu Deity Everybody Admires
author: Paul Younger
target_audience: Readers interested in Hinduism and Indian religion
Scholars and students of religious studies or anthropology
Collectors and enthusiasts of religious iconography
Those interested in cross-cultural and global traditions
core_themes: Universality and adaptability of the Ganesha image
The personal and collective devotion surrounding Ganesha
Transformation of religious icons in global contexts
primary_purpose: To document and reflect on the author's experiences collecting Ganesha images worldwide, exploring the religious, artistic, and cultural meanings of Ganesha representations and their appeal across diverse communities.

structure_format.organization: Arranged as a series of personal essays and anecdotes, interspersed with photographs and commentary on collected images
features: Travel narrative intertwining personal quest and academic insight
Full-color photographs and descriptions of Ganesha images
Historical and cultural context for the representations encountered

key_concepts_lessons: Ganesha’s image is globally omnipresent and adaptable across contexts, religions, and cultures.
The act of collecting religious images can serve as a deep exploration of material faith and personal spiritual journey.
Ganesha’s accessibility and charm contribute to his popularity among devotees and non-devotees alike.
Cultural and historical layers are embedded in variations of Ganesha representations.
Observing objects of devotion outside their traditional contexts reveals broader patterns of religious transmission and transformation.
notable_features: Richly illustrated with photographs of Ganesha statues and images from around the world
Blends travel writing with scholarly analysis
Focuses on lived religion and everyday devotion
Explores intersections between art, faith, and cultural exchange
cultural_historical_context: Emerging at a time of increasing global mobility and intercultural exchange, the book both records and participates in the worldwide spread of Hindu motifs, particularly Ganesha, after decades of diaspora and curiosity in Eastern spirituality outside India.
reception_impact: Praised for its engaging, accessible approach to scholarship
Valued by scholars and devotees for its blend of personal observation and academic insight
Used as a resource to illustrate the global reach of South Asian religious imagery
Seen as a celebration of religious pluralism and everyday spirituality
comparable_titles: Ganesa: Lord of Obstacles, Lord of Beginnings by Paul B. Courtright
Nine Lives: In Search of the Sacred in Modern India by William Dalrymple
The Life of Hinduism (The Life of Religion) edited by John Stratton Hawley and Vasudha Narayanan
The Hindu Religious Tradition by Thomas J. Hopkins
